Katalog Berita (Halaman 49/56)

#1598. Opinion: Key Liverpool defender is staying and it's not Virgil van Dijk

Liverpool's squad is a bit broken in some places at the moment.

On paper, it feels like they should have one of the best teams in the Premier League but, they're currently fourth in the table.

Obviously, there have been some games where their true colours have shone through but, more often than not, they've been left behind by their title rivals.

Manchester City and Arsenal are the two teams who have beaten them in the England's top flight with their third defeat coming against Fenerbahce in the Champions League a couple of weeks ago.

These aren't the performance levels that fans were expecting from their team but, they seem to be the ones they're being handed.

So, for things to get better, decisions need to be made about the future of Liverpool's first-team squad and now, it finally feels like the Reds have been given their answer about the future of one star.

James Pearce more or less confirms Joe Gomez is staying at Anfield

This summer, the improvement of Liverpool's defence was one of their main concerns.

Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley let Arne Slot's men down on more than one occasion last term which resulted in Dominik Szoboszlai and Curtis Jones being used there instead.

And, while they did well, both midfielders performed a lot better when used in their natural positions.

Slot still got them to qualify for the Champions League by the skin of his teeth but, in reality, fans thought that he'd do a lot more after his £450 million spend in the transfer window.

Evidently, that wasn't the case and even though they added a couple of new faces to their back line this summer, it's unclear whether that'll be enough or not.

But, thanks to a fresh update from James Pearce, Liverpool's plans for Joe Gomez have been made clear.

"Centre-back not a priority for Liverpool so highly unlikely they will invest heavily in that area either in Jan or next summer. Jacquet has made a huge impact and big hopes for fellow young CBs Leoni, Ndukwe and Ndiaye," he wrote.

Joe Gomez staying at Liverpool is very good news

Over the last few years, Gomez's role within Liverpool's starting XI has diminished.

The centre-back is now the Reds' longest-serving player and, without him, they'd not be where they are today.

Before his ACL injury a few years ago, he was on course to becoming one of England's best centre-backs.

However, his injury unfortunately stunted his progress and caused him to become a bench warmer.

Since then, he's adapted his game quite a bit and he can now play in any position across the back four.

This versatility is probably one of the main things that have kept him around because, his injury list has just been getting longer and longer each year.

Obviously, if a new centre-back isn't going to be coming in, Gomez needs to stay but, with his contract set to expire in June, the Reds must quickly decide how long they want to keep him on for.

If Gomez can stay fit, he could become a regular feature among Liverpool's ranks again but, if he doesn't, it would be pointless handing him a new deal.

Here's hoping that the Reds won't live to regret this decision.

By Darren Plant | 13 Nov 2026 17:31

Pedro Neto has claimed that Chelsea teammate Moises Caicedo is under-appreciated.

In the absence of the injured Reece James, Caicedo has spent time as Blues captain under new manager Xabi Alonso.

The midfielder is currently with Ecuador, the 25-year-old having revealed this week that he is prepared to play through the pain barrier for his country.

If Caicedo remains in South America until after Tuesday's friendly against Bolivia, it will put his availability for the Premier League fixture versus Leeds United on November 21 in considerable doubt.

Speaking in an interview with O Jogo, Neto has suggested that he always wants to be lining up with Caicedo in his team.

Neto claims that the former Brighton & Hove Albion player brings "security" to Chelsea.

"People don’t talk about him much, but they should give him more credit. Maybe he’s paid the price for a season that didn’t go well for the team, but he’s a complete player."

As someone who has only contributed eight goals and 11 assists in 155 matches for Chelsea, Caicedo needs to excel in the defensive side of the game.

Generally-speaking, Chelsea's performance level should rise with Caicedo in it, but he has recently completed 90 minutes in defeats to Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland.

Chelsea were outplayed and outfought in both matches, and it served as a reminder that Caicedo should not necessarily be viewed as one of the best midfielders on the planet right now.

Alonso needs to find a way for Caicedo to strike up an effective partnership with either Romeo Lavia or Jordan Henderson over the coming months.

#1594. Report: Liverpool star ready to agree new long-term deal

Liverpool have a lot of contract decisions to make over the next few months.

But, when the January transfer window is open, any players who aren't tied down to contracts will be able to speak to foreign clubs about a free transfer.

Virgil van Dijk, Alisson and even Joe Gomez have all been linked with moves away next summer with several clubs vying for the transfer of each player.

However, outside of those who's contracts are going to expire in June, some of their best players are also on the verge of receiving new deals as their contracts are also set to expire in the next couple of years with one agreement now being confirmed.

Rio Ngumoha is ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool

Last season, Rio Ngumoha was one of the only success stories to emerge from Anfield.

The 18-year-old managed to fight his way into Iraola's starting XI and, he even bagged his first-ever Premier League goal.

Since then, many different rumours have emerged about his future with Bayern Munich even being interested in signing him.

Obviously, that didn't end up happening and, instead, he got given a regular first-team role in Iraola's squad and has already featured in 14 games this term.

This added experience coupled with the two assists he's chipped in with in the Champions League have all helped him cement his place at Anfield.

However, his contract runs out in 2028 so, a new deal needs to be agreed with him soon and, according to Football Insider, that is exactly what's about to happen.

"Rio Ngumoha will likely end speculation linking him away by signing a new contract at Liverpool, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 18-year-old has starred for the Reds this season, emerging as a key player for Andoni Iraola's side.

"But with his current terms set to expire in 2028, decision-makers at Anfield have faced mounting pressure to tie the England international down to a new deal.

"Ngumoha is happy at Liverpool and ready to put pen to paper.

"The winger has also broken into Thomas Tuchel's England squad this season, featuring off the bench in Thursday's 2-1 win over Croatia.

"Liverpool eventually paid a fee in the region of £6.8million for the teenager, who joined the club from Chelsea in 2024."

Rio Ngumoha is the future of Liverpool's attack

Liverpool have a lot of attackers among their ranks at the moment.

However, some are performing much better than others.

Alexander Isak is still the Reds' most expensive signing ever and, even though he has chipped in with a couple of goals so far, he could be doing a lot better.

The same goes for Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz.

However, Ngumoha and Cody Gakpo have performed extremely well. In fact, Gakpo is probably the Reds' best-performing attacker right now, even if he has suffered an injury or two.

Obviously, Gakpo is a lot older than Ngumoha but, if the Englishman manages to learn a thing or two from his senior teammate, he'd become even better than he already is.

And, since he's already seen as the next big thing at Liverpool, this new contract just confirms it.

Here's hoping that these rumours are true and, before the end of the season, Liverpool announce his new deal.

#1593. Sebastian Pocognoli targets Tottenham star for Scotland allegiance switch from England

By Ben Sully | 13 Nov 2026 17:36, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 17:38

Scotland Sebastien Pocognoli has admitted Tottenham Hotspur star Archie Gray is one of two Premier League players he is targeting for a potential allegiance switch from England.

Gray is currently with the England Under-21 squad after working his way through the national team age groups.

Barring any injury issues, the 20-year-old is likely to be part of Lee Carsley's squad for the Under-21 European Championships next summer.

However, progression to the England senior side is far from a foregone conclusion, partly because he is also eligible to represent Scotland.

Gray's father, Andy, represented Scotland at senior level, as did his grandfather, Frank, and his great-uncle, Eddie.

Pocognoli has admitted Gray and Everton's Hayden Hackney are his radar for potential allegiance switches to Scotland, who have not been put off by failing to convince Harvey Barnes to represent the Tartan Army under Steve Clarke.

“With Barnes it was different," Pocognoli said. "I knew before my first camp that he was different.

"The two other lads [Gray and Hackney] are young lads. It’s a long way. But if you wait too long, it might not be the right moment. In a year’s time, we will see.

“Right now, we have players in the squad who are performing well. It will always be up to them to be the priority.

"Because we’ve built things and we’ve had time with the ones who are here right now. But we are on it. We are always proactive in all of these situations.

"What is very exciting about those two names is that they are young players. That’s interesting. We have to look and manage the situation.”

Everton's Hackney made a couple of appearances for Scotland Under-21 side before going on to feature 13 times for the England Under-21s.

The 24-year-old now has to decide whether he will commit to England or Scotland, with Pocognoli feeling that the best route to convincing players like Hackney is by giving them a project to believe in.

“The best way to convince players is to show good football, show them they can come to us, enjoy it and be successful," the Scotland boss added.

“They have to feel when they leave a top club that they arrive here into top conditions and a top environment. That’s the best publicity we can offer, to show good football.”

Scotland will return to action against North Macedonia this evening, before they conclude the UEFA Nations League league phase with a game against Switzerland on Sunday.

#1592. Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

James pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Late free-kick for Leeds after Livramento bundled Aaronson over. Wilson chips from the left to the far post and Muharemovic heads it back acros goal looking for a team-mate but none had made the run.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 1 (Touré) No clean sheet for Leeds. Farke is fuming after the substitute exploits an error and scores with a left-foot shot that deflects off Justin.

Livramento drives the ball 60 yards looking for Barnes but the ball skids off the turf and into Trafford’s arms.

Crunching Bard tackle on Bamba sends the ball to James who lets fly from 22 yards into the shins of a Newcastle defender.

Bard is penalised for a trip on Barnes as the game peters out.

Ampadu and Bamba collide when fighting for a loose ball but there was nothing malicious in it.

Wissa escapes a booking for a snide kick at Muharemovic’s shin.

A debatable offside call which should have been left for VAR lets Trafford off the hook when he comes out of his area to clear a ball clipped over the top. He slices it to Toure and the ref stops the game but I think Bard was playing Wissa, who found Toure, onside.

Newcastle corner on the left headed out by Elvedi and Barnes recovers the ball to start another attack with the 18-yard line stacked with players. When the diagonal comes back from left to right Barnes heads it behind for a goalkick.

Willock hooks a half-volley on to the roof of the net.

Bard → GudmundssonAaronson → OkaforWilson → Tanaka

Newcastle free-kick for a trip on Willock. Hall takes and Leeds head it out for a throw-in.

Livramento improves the quality of crosses with two that at least find the middle of the box even if they were headed away by Elvedi and Justin respectively.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

Barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

There was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

Newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

These are early days but this performance and result had been coming. A pretty brutal reality check after all the positive noise and bold predictions in pre-season. This defeat will drop Newcastle to 12th in the table, where they finished last season under Eddie Howe.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 0 (Okafor) Ampadu hurls it into the box. A defender heads it to the edge of the area where Okafor thumps a left-footed half-volley in off the right post.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Livramento slides in to stop Okafor’s drive down the left, giving Leeds another opportunity to throw it long.

Triple change: Livramento → DedicTouré → Fernandez-PardoWillock → Murphy

Leeds catch Newcastle playing short from the back. Stach blindsides Steur 20 yards out, tackles him, cuts inside then bends a left foot shot into the side-netting.

After Hall stings Trafford’s palms with a strike from distance. Newcastle want a penalty when the ball hits Tanaka’s arm … but it was outside the area and then Murphy, in frustration, chops down Gudmundsson and takes the booking as an occupational hazard.

Elvedi sloppily gives the ball way to Wissa who tries to set Fernandez-Pardo through down the left. Justin sticks with him and Bogle mops up after Justin was tripped.

Gudmundsson does the upended beetle when he tries to break from the corner and collides with a Newcastle player. He claims he was fouled and wthrashes about like a RL player after he’s tackled. He continues to do a Rumpelstiltskin polka of peevishness towards the ref for a while.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

No changes at half-time for Newcastle as they kick off. Leeds break through the middle quickly and Calvert-Lewin seems to push the ball past Botman and shapes to shoot before Steur slides in with a crucial tackle just inside the box.

The first goal is now an own goal. The explanation is that Tanaka’s shot was on target but the deflection from Steur meant it was going wide until it hit Miley.

Now the second goal has been credited to Bogle as Calvert-Lewin’s header struck the top of his head before it went in.

You could not say that this scoreline is undeserved. Newcastle are being demolished physically. The central midfield two – Steur and Miley – just don’t have the power to screen their defence.

Leeds 3 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds are running all over Newcastle who seem physically flimsy. Calvert-Lewin chops in from the left on to a flick-on, the ball takes a deflection off the Newcastle captain and he steers it into the far corner with a right-foot shot.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

Calvert-Lewin is booked for catching Botman in the face with a straight arm rather than a swinging arm. ‘Reckless but not violent.’ Trafford had punchd the corner away at the back post to set Leeds off on a counter.

Tanaka gives the ball away carelessly in midfield and Newcastle work it to Wissa who chops inside past Elvedi, hangs out his own leg looking for contact and hits the deck. The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

Newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

For those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

Leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

Leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

Leeds 1 Newcastle 0 (Tanaka) Good move, spawny finish. Tanaka sprays a pass out to Okafor who drives at Dedic then picks out Tanaka who had held his run. He cushions the pass then lets fly. Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

It almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not currently have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

Newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

From the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

Newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

Justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

Leeds have been the slicker of the two sides, their passing and movement causing the full-backs problems. Okafor dribbles down the left and centres. Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

Newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

Wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. Leeds shift it quickly out to the left with Gudmundsson and Okafor bombing forward. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

Two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

He got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the new striker.

It’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

Leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

#1591. Real Madrid's Endrick faces Donyell Malen dilemma over Roma loan

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 17:58

Real Madrid forward Endrick could find an attractive route back to regular football at Roma in January, but the remarkable form of former Aston Villa attacker Donyell Malen raises questions over the Brazilian's potential role under Gian Piero Gasperini.

The 20-year-old has struggled for opportunities since returning from his successful loan spell at Lyon, managing just 141 minutes across seven appearances for Real Madrid this season.

Roma remain interested in signing him on loan when the transfer window reopens, having already attempted to secure his services during the summer before Jose Mourinho blocked the move.

However, a potential switch to the Italian capital presents an intriguing sporting dilemma. Malen has established himself as one of Serie A's most productive forwards, scoring eight goals in his first 10 league appearances of the 2026-27 campaign.

For Endrick, whose main priority is securing consistent playing time, joining a team with such an established attacking figure could carry a familiar risk.

Malen has been outstanding since joining Roma from Aston Villa in January 2026, scoring 14 goals in 18 Serie A appearances during the second half of last season.

The Netherlands international has maintained that impressive form under Gasperini, adding eight league goals and four Champions League strikes this term.

His performances have made him a central figure in Roma's attacking system, with the Italian side emerging as genuine contenders near the top of Serie A after finishing third last season.

The competition for Endrick would therefore be considerable, particularly if he arrived expecting to operate as the team's first-choice centre-forward.

Yet an analysis published by Brazilian outlet Trivela suggests that Gasperini's tactical approach could offer the Real Madrid youngster opportunities beyond the traditional number nine position.

Roma generally operate with three central defenders, attacking wing-backs and two supporting forwards behind a central striker.

Their emphasis on aggressive pressing, direct attacking movements and exploiting spaces behind opposition defences could suit Endrick's explosive acceleration and ability to finish quickly.

Rather than competing exclusively with Malen, the Brazilian could potentially operate alongside him as a second striker, receiving possession between the lines before driving towards goal.

Malen's movement across the forward line would also provide opportunities for Endrick to attack spaces created by the Dutchman's positioning.

Such an arrangement would require tactical adjustments from Gasperini, however, and there has been no indication that the Roma manager has guaranteed Endrick a particular role.

The Italian club also possess other attacking options, including Paulo Dybala, Matias Soule and Rodrigo Mora, meaning the youngster would still face competition even if deployed behind Malen.

Interestingly, the two forwards were both on the scoresheet when Real Madrid secured a dramatic 4-3 Champions League victory over Roma on October 14.

Malen struck twice for the hosts, while Endrick came off the bench to score Madrid's equaliser before Antonio Rudiger completed the comeback.

Endrick's situation at Real Madrid has become increasingly difficult despite his encouraging performances during last season's loan at Lyon.

The former Palmeiras youngster scored eight goals in 21 appearances in France, demonstrating how regular involvement could accelerate his development.

His limited opportunities under Mourinho have since prompted renewed speculation about another temporary departure.

Speaking while on international duty with Brazil earlier this week, Endrick acknowledged that his immediate priority was simply to play more regularly.

"I just want to play. I want to be happy, to help my teammates... to score goals and provide assists, just as I did at Lyon, which was one of the best things that's ever happened to me and one of the happiest times of my life," he told reporters.

"I don't know what will happen in January. That's in God's hands. I'm only 20 and I'll see what happens. I just ask to do what's best for my career."

Roma's interest remains genuine, with La Repubblica reporting this week that the club are monitoring the Brazilian's situation as they consider January attacking reinforcements.

However, Sporting Lisbon have also emerged as serious contenders for Endrick's signature, with former Lyon manager Paulo Fonseca reportedly keen on a reunion.

That connection could prove significant, given the improvement Endrick showed during their previous spell together in France.

Meanwhile, Mourinho's previous decision to reject Roma's approach remains another obstacle, with Real Madrid yet to approve a January departure.

Roma can offer Champions League football, a competitive Serie A environment and a tactical system that appears suited to Endrick's attacking qualities.

Whether those advantages outweigh the prospect of competing with Malen for minutes could be crucial if the Italian club succeed in reopening negotiations.

For a player who has started just once for Real Madrid this season, the possibility of playing alongside Roma's leading scorer may be appealing, but any January decision will also depend on how regularly Gasperini can accommodate him.

#1589. Report: Bayern Munich sensation now 'extremely high' on Liverpool's shortlist

Liverpool have a lot of issues within their squad that need resolving.

The Anfield outfit may have spent over £150 million trying to improve each area of their team but, they've still ended up fourth in the Premier League table.

Granted, we're only 10 games into the season at the moment but, their performances have seemed to be the same since the start of the campaign.

They seem to be able to easily beat teams who are noticeably weaker than them (aside from Fenerbahce) while they struggle against teams who are noticeably better than them such as Arsenal and Manchester City.

This has made it clear that more talent needs to be added to Liverpool's ranks with another player now entering the mix.

Liverpool have set their eyes on Bayern Munich starlet, Tom Bischof

Midfield and full-back are the two main areas that Liverpool have been lacking in this season.

Indeed, there have been some games when the players in those positions have performed well but, more often than not, they've played well below expectations.

This has led to many different players being linked with an Anfield switch and now, yet another player has entered the equation.

"In addition to Pablo Barrios, Bayern Munich’s Tom Bischof remains extremely high on #LFC’s radar, as reported several weeks ago, with further developments now emerging behind the scenes," ITK Space wrote.

"Liverpool’s scouting department regard the German as one of Europe’s most exceptional emerging midfield talents, with his increasing involvement at Bayern this season only strengthening an already outstanding internal assessment.

"Remarkably, some within the club are understood to rank Bischof even ahead of Pablo Barrios in their internal evaluations, with an exchange of information having already taken place with Germany’s new national team manager Jürgen Klopp, who handed Bischof his senior international debut and is understood to regard him as a cornerstone of Germany’s midfield for the next decade.

"Furthermore, Bischof has already made contact with Florian Wirtz to gain a deeper understanding of life at Liverpool, the atmosphere within the dressing room and the environment surrounding the club, adding another fascinating dimension to a developing story in which Liverpool's admiration extends considerably beyond routine scouting interest."

Tom Bischof is one of the most versatile players that Liverpool can sign

Versatility is one of the most important things that a footballer can have in their locker in this day and age.

The ability to play in multiple positions is not only helpful for the club but, it also means that the player is likely to get more chances to play.

Whether they're used in their preferred position or not is another question but, the fact that most players can now comfortably be used in more than one position is a sign of the times changing.

Bischof is probably a player that most people outside of the Bundesliga wont have heard of but, throughout his career, he's played in almost every position except from striker and centre-back.

Recently, he's honed his skills on three specific positions, left-back, right-back and central midfield.

All three of these positions are where Liverpool need upgrades this term so, signing one player who can cover all three would be huge.

Obviously, change is afoot this January with Liverpool still miles behind their title rivals.

So, if Bischof can be bought, he should definitely be one of the first transfers that Iraola and Julian Ward make, especially because he's only 21 years old and has already featured in 172 games throughout his career.

By Ben Sully | 13 Nov 2026 18:03, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 18:30

Arsenal reportedly have identified AC Milan attacker Alphadjo Cisse as a potential transfer target.

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta currently has a number of options for who can play in the three behind the central striker, including Noni Madueke, Christos Tzolis, Martin Odegaard, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka, although the latter is currently sidelined with an injury.

Despite boasting those options, Arsenal attempted to add Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior to their attacking department in the summer.

However, they ultimately failed in their pursuit of the Brazilian, who decided to sign a new long-term contract with Los Blancos.

With that in mind, Arsenal are likely to revisit their pursuit of attacking reinforcements in the upcoming transfer windows.

According to Tuttomercatoweb, the Gunners have identified Milan's Cisse as a potential target for their future transfer business.

The Premier League leaders are said to be showing 'strong interest' in Cisse, along with Brighton & Hove Albion.

The report also claims other clubs have made enquiries about the possibility of signing the Milan youngster.

The Italian giants are said to value Cisse in the region of €50m (£41.8m) to €60m (£50m) for an attacker who is under contract until June 2030.

Cisse started his senior career with Hellas Verona before joining Serie B side Catanzaro on loan in the summer of 2025.

After being impressed with Cisse's performances, Milan swooped in to secure his signature at the start of February before loaning him back to Catanzaro.

Having since linked up with the Rossoneri, the highly-rated talent has quickly adapted to life as a top-flight footballer, having netted five goals in Serie A appearances.

The 20-year-old also scored his first senior hat-trick in a 4-0 win over Red Bull Salzburg in last month's Europa League clash.

Cisse, who recently earned a call-up to Roberto Mancini's Italy squad, has primarily been used as an attacking midfielder by Ruben Amorim this season, but he is capable of playing slightly deeper, out wide and even as a striker.

#1586. Report: Future of Liverpool sensation unclear, he could be axed

Liverpool have a lot of players within their squad.

However, as has always been the case, certain players are preferred over others.

But, with Andoni Iraola being brought in to replace Arne Slot, some subtle changes were made to the Reds' first-team plans.

For example, if Slot was still in charge, Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and James McConnell would have all been loaned out and forgotten about.

But, with the Spaniard in charge, that has not been the case. Some questions have been raised about what the future holds for certain Liverpool players but, for one sensation, it's still rather unclear.

Valencia could still end up terminating Harvey Elliott's loan early

Harvey Elliott's Liverpool career has been a bit like a rollercoaster.

The Englishman started off his time at Anfield as one of the first names on Jurgen Klopp's team sheet.

Granted, he did spend a season out on loan to Blackburn Rovers but, aside from then, he was often kept in and around Liverpool's starting XI.

However, since Slot and Iraola have been in charge, things haven't quite gone to plan for the midfielder.

He did win the Premier League title with the club during the 2024-25 campaign but, the season after, he was shipped out on loan to Aston Villa where he failed to meet expectations and only featured in nine games.

This term, the same thing has happened again as, even though he's one of Valencia's highest-paid players, he's not met the standards expected of him.

Elliott's lack of form has caused all sorts of rumours to emerge with journalist German Munoz now sharing an update on the Englishman's current situation.

"Valencia’s winter transfer window situation. Braulio has no plans to overhaul the squad by moving out key players, but he will try to offload players who get little playing time to free up more room for signings," he wrote.

"Elliot: very high wages; if his level doesn’t improve, there is a possibility of terminating his loan in January if Liverpool agree."

Harvey Elliott must do everything he can to get his Liverpool career back on track

Elliott's career started off with so much expectation but, right now, it feels like he's plateauing.

Indeed, he did manage to have a rather impressive Euros with England's Under-21's last summer but, that clearly wasn't enough.

This season-long loan with Valencia is probably the last chance that Elliott is going to get to prove his worth to Liverpool.

He's 23 years old now and, even though he's versatile and can be used as a midfielder or a winger, that's not enough to earn him a place in Iraola's plans.

That is, despite the fact he'd be classed as homegrown at club which, is exactly what Liverpool need right now.

If Elliott doesn't turn things around soon, it's hard to see what his next step will be, so, here's hoping that he can replicate his recent Copa del Rey performance in the future.

#1585. Barcelona's Deco targets Brazilian first-team star in five-year plan

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 18:18

Barcelona's new partnership with Brazilian academy Sfera FC comes with an ambitious target: developing at least one player capable of reaching the Catalan club's first team within the next five years.

The objective was revealed by Sfera co-founder and chief executive Gustavo Aranha in an exclusive interview with Trivela, offering fresh insight into the agreement recently negotiated by Barcelona sporting director Deco.

The two clubs announced a five-year collaboration earlier this month, giving Barcelona preferential access to emerging Brazilian talents while allowing young players to experience the training environment at La Masia.

However, Aranha has now explained that the project extends well beyond identifying potential transfer targets, with Sfera hoping to establish a direct pathway from its academy in Sao Paulo to Barcelona's senior squad.

"Beyond that, the main objective is to have at least one player developed by Sfera playing in Barcelona's first team within five years," Aranha told Trivela.

It is an ambition set by the Brazilian club rather than a guarantee from Barcelona, whose agreement contains no obligation to sign players or promote them to the senior side.

The agreement originated from a visit Deco made to Sfera's training facilities in May, although the former Barcelona midfielder was already familiar with the organisation before becoming the club's sporting director.

Aranha explained that the visit helped transform their existing relationship into formal negotiations, eventually resulting in a five-season contract.

Established in 2021, Sfera specialises in developing young footballers rather than operating as a conventional professional club.

Its academy currently works with players from under-11 to under-19 level, and the organisation has no intention of establishing a senior team.

"Our partners and I never wanted to have a traditional football club. We wanted to build the best player development process in Brazil," Aranha explained.

Barcelona's involvement provides a significant opportunity for that model, particularly given the competition among European clubs to identify promising Brazilian youngsters before their market values increase.

Under the agreement, Barcelona will receive priority when assessing players developed by Sfera, with the two organisations working together to identify individuals suited to the Catalans' sporting requirements.

Nevertheless, the Spanish giants are under no contractual obligation to complete any transfers.

Aranha also confirmed that the clubs deliberately rejected the idea of setting a minimum number of players to be sent to Barcelona each season.

Such a requirement could have resulted in youngsters being recommended before they were ready, while also potentially restricting opportunities if Sfera produced an especially promising generation.

The partnership does not prevent the Brazilian academy from maintaining relationships with other clubs, either.

"The Barcelona partnership is not about them coming to Sfera to teach us how to develop players according to their methodology," Aranha added.

"They want Sfera to continue doing its work, using the institutional relationship to enhance and showcase our players."

For Deco, the arrangement offers a more direct connection to a Brazilian development programme without Barcelona needing to establish or operate their own academy in the country.

One of the most distinctive aspects of the agreement concerns the possibility of Sfera players making repeated visits to Barcelona before any permanent transfer is considered.

Rather than inviting youngsters to Spain for a conventional trial, the clubs intend to create a gradual process of assessment and adaptation.

Sfera will recommend players based on their development and individual characteristics, while Barcelona's coaching staff will assess whether they meet the club's requirements.

Selected youngsters could then spend several weeks training at La Masia before returning to Brazil with specific areas of their game to improve.

"It's not about a definitive trial where a player goes there and stays, but about building an adaptation process through several visits," Aranha explained.

"That way, Barcelona get to know the player closely, and we understand which areas we need to focus on developing when he returns."

This approach is designed to prepare youngsters for the demands of European football before they face the additional pressures of a permanent move abroad.

It could be particularly valuable when players approach the transition to Barcelona's under-19 or reserve teams.

The agreement also includes exchanges between coaching staff, allowing Sfera employees to observe La Masia's training methods and incorporate relevant lessons into their work in Brazil.

Aranha stressed that the Brazilian club would retain its own identity, rather than becoming a Barcelona satellite academy.

Sfera's development model places considerable importance on education, emotional development and individual support alongside conventional technical and physical preparation.

Players undergo weekly video analysis sessions, while the academy also aims to develop their decision-making and understanding of the game.

For Barcelona, the potential reward is early access to youngsters who have already experienced the club's footballing environment.

For Sfera, the ultimate measure of success would be seeing one of those players progress through the academy system and eventually represent the senior side.

The five-year agreement includes the possibility of an extension, although Aranha believes the relationship should ultimately be judged by the quality of the players developed and the opportunities created.

No specific youngster has yet been identified as the potential beneficiary of that first-team ambition, but the partnership gives Barcelona a structured route to monitor the next generation of Brazilian talent long before a permanent transfer becomes necessary.

#1584. Man City face £35m French goalkeeper demand as Liverpool and Man United join race

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 18:48

Manchester City are reportedly preparing a £26m move for Lens goalkeeper Robin Risser, but the Premier League giants face a significant financial obstacle as Liverpool and Manchester United also monitor the highly-rated French international.

The 21-year-old has emerged as one of the most sought-after young goalkeepers in European football following his rapid development at Lens, where he established himself as first choice after arriving from Strasbourg in the summer of 2025.

According to Swiss outlet 4-4-2.ch, City are leading the interest in Risser and have been scouting him for some time, with a potential offer of €30m (£26m) under consideration ahead of next summer's transfer window.

However, Lens are reportedly demanding at least €40m (£35m) for the France international, who remains under contract until June 2030.

Liverpool and Manchester United are also keeping close tabs on his situation, while Italian giants Inter Milan and Juventus have joined the list of potential suitors.

Risser's emergence represents a remarkable piece of recruitment by Lens, who paid Strasbourg just €3m (£2.6m), plus potential bonuses, to secure his signature in July 2025.

The former Red Star loanee quickly established himself under Pierre Sage, helping Lens finish second in Ligue 1 and win their first Coupe de France during the 2025-26 campaign.

His performances also earned him a place in Didier Deschamps's France squad for the 2026 World Cup, although he has yet to make his senior international debut.

New national team manager Zinedine Zidane has retained faith in the youngster, selecting him for November's Nations League fixtures against Italy and Turkey.

At 6ft 4in, Risser possesses the physical attributes expected of a modern goalkeeper, combining an imposing aerial presence with composure in possession and the ability to initiate attacks from the back.

Those qualities have reportedly attracted Manchester City's attention, although the proposed transfer fee could complicate their pursuit.

Lens have another financial consideration when assessing potential offers, as Strasbourg negotiated a sell-on clause when Risser moved between the two Ligue 1 clubs.

While 4-4-2.ch reports that Strasbourg would receive 25% of any future transfer fee, French newspaper L'Equipe previously described the clause as 25% of the profit generated by a subsequent sale.

The precise terms have not been publicly confirmed, but the arrangement would reduce the amount Lens could retain from a major transfer.

That provides additional context for their reported £35m asking price, which would represent an enormous increase on the goalkeeper's original acquisition cost.

Despite his growing reputation, Risser has experienced a considerably more difficult start to the current campaign.

Lens have conceded 31 goals in 15 matches across all competitions, including a humiliating 9-1 Champions League defeat against Como earlier this month.

Nevertheless, his international recognition and long-term potential appear to have maintained the interest of several leading European clubs.

Manchester City's reported interest is particularly intriguing given the presence of Gianluigi Donnarumma, who remains the established first-choice goalkeeper under Enzo Maresca.

The Italian international has been a key figure since joining from Paris Saint-Germain, meaning Risser would face considerable competition for regular opportunities if he moved to the Etihad Stadium.

Any potential deal could therefore be viewed as a long-term investment, although there is currently no suggestion that City are planning to replace Donnarumma.

Liverpool's interest raises a different question, with uncertainty surrounding the long-term future of Alisson Becker potentially encouraging the Reds to assess younger alternatives.

The Brazilian has remained an important figure at Anfield, but Risser's age and experience in both Ligue 1 and the Champions League make him an attractive prospect for clubs planning beyond their current number ones.

Manchester United are also understood to be monitoring the Frenchman despite already having Senne Lammens in their squad.

Neither Liverpool nor United have been reported to have submitted a formal offer, and their interest remains at the monitoring stage.

Risser has previously attracted attention from other Premier League clubs, with Newcastle United making initial contact with his representatives in March.

Tottenham Hotspur were also linked with the goalkeeper earlier this year as they considered alternatives to Guglielmo Vicario.

The latest reports suggest that Lens could face a considerably more competitive market for Risser next summer, with Inter and Juventus providing additional interest from Serie A.

For Manchester City, the immediate issue is whether they are prepared to meet Lens's £35m valuation or negotiate a lower fee for a goalkeeper whose contract still has more than three years remaining.

With the French club under no immediate pressure to sell, their reported asking price may prove the decisive obstacle to any deal.

#1582. Paul Scholes calls Man United's bizarre lap of honour 'embarrassing' after Gary Neville claimed stars are risking 'emotional damage' with post-match ritual

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER

Published: 04:05 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 11:18 EST, 11 November 2026

Paul Scholes has branded Manchester United's post-match walks of honour 'embarrassing' after Gary Neville suggested the squad are causing themselves 'emotional damage'.

United staged another incredible fightback to snatch a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford after trailing by two goals heading into injury-time.

But it wasn't enough to spare the club from the humiliation of being in the relegation zone for the next two weeks – the longest United have spent there since 1986.

After the full-time whistle, the United players conducted a post-match walk of honour as the fans chanted Michael Carrick's name in a defiant show of support for their beleaguered boss – a move a number of ex-United stars have called into question.

'I tell you one thing they have to do, is stop these laps of honour after the game,' Scholes said, speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite. 'What the f***?'

Nicky Butt added: 'It's p***ing me off,' before Scholes continued: 'They are so bad. Not so much Michael, the team as well. It's embarrassing. It should be after the last game of the season. I feel sorry for them.'

Paul Scholes has torn into Manchester United for their regular post-match laps of honour (Source: YouTube/The Good, The Bad and The Football)

Gary Neville, meanwhile, said the habit has become 'painful to watch' as a United fan

Neville, meanwhile, said on NBC Sports: 'You have got to admire their persistence, they kept going. 'Defensive errors were shocking and we'll discuss that shortly. But this lap around the pitch...

'I played for Manchester United 602 times and I always appreciated the fans at the end of the game, but this pattern of them walking around the pitch after defeats by Bournemouth and a 4-4 at home against Aston Villa, it's almost painful to watch. They're almost causing themselves emotional damage.

'This just can't go on, can it? It's absolutely desperate. Michael will be proud of them and the fans are singing his name because they love him but this is a really sorry situation.'

Carrick was involved in a spiky back-and-forth with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison when it was suggested to him that he could step down:

Davison: 'What do you expect to happen over the next few weeks? If you thought walking away was the best thing, you'd probably do it.'

Davison: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

Carrick: 'You're telling me what you think, aren't you?'

Davison: 'I'm asking you what you think? What do you expect to happen?'

Carrick: 'We understand the situation; we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward and keep working on things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.'

He added: 'Michael will be proud of them and the fans are singing his name because they love him but this is a really sorry situation' (Source: YouTube/NBC Sports)

Carrick insisted 'it's not going to happen' when it was put to him that he could walk away if he thought that would be the 'best thing' for the club

Then, speaking in his post-match press conference, Carrick expressed confidence his side could still turn things around this season.

'One hundred per cent,' he said. 'I think there's more than enough. Goals change games and we've got to deal with it and it's something we have to improve on drastically. But there's more than enough, we're just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times…

'I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in. We've just got to win games.'

Amid a wave of fan protests expressing their discontent towards INEOS and the Glazer family on Sunday, Neville has suggested that the club's hierarchy 'don't have a clue what to do' on Carrick.

He added: 'You can keep changing the manager and thinking that's going to be the answer. But this has been proven now over eight managers in 12 years - that's not the answer.

'Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don't know. The ownership don't have a clue what to do.

'It's rinse and repeat. (Ruben) Amorim, (Erik) Ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick - some of them are world-class managers who have had success; there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex-players who know the club as well.

'None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you've got a poor performance department, a poor recruitment department, you've not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club, you will fail.

'Every organisation in the world will fail if you've not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom - your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch trying to play football.

'There are real issues within that football club; you've got people doing those jobs who have never done those jobs before in senior positions.'

#1581. "Best team in the world" Spain will have too much for England in fascinating Nations League affair

By Matt Law | 13 Nov 2026 19:17, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 19:21

Ahead of Spain's UEFA Nations League clash with England on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses La Roja's chances of success.

It's an outstanding team. March 2024 was the last time they lost. They did lose to Portugal in the Nations League final on penalties, but technically that counts as a draw, so it doesn't work against them in terms of this record.

They are just the outstanding team in the world, let alone Europe, and the clear number one in world football at the moment.

That win the other night against Czechia epitomised everything that they could do without their best player, and without Oyarzabal, who's been fantastic for them.

Laporte and Rodri were missing too. But they put a team on the field, and you look at the team and you say, "It's a really good team."

On paper, they had Yeremy Pino and Alex Baena, Fermin Lopez and Ferran Torres, and don't get me wrong, these are wonderful players, but it's not Kylian Mbappe, it's not Lamine Yamal, it's not Harry Kane.

Those forwards are not at the top of world football. But as a team, they get the job done.

They didn't really have to break sweat in that 2-0 win on Thursday, which put them on five wins from five in the section. It's an outstanding team, and one that will be strengthened by Lamine Yamal. He had a slight knee injury.

I wonder how much of an injury it was, or whether, after that Barcelona-Atletico game, they just decided to give him a bit of a rest for the Czechia game because they felt like they could win without him.

He's coming back into the squad, and Luis de la Fuente said that he's in excellent shape for this game, so I'm fully expecting him to come back into the starting side.

Oyarzabal had an illness and also stayed behind for the birth of his second child, so he will join up with the squad as well.

He's a player I really like and someone I've watched a lot of in La Liga. He's had an excellent record for Spain, with 31 goals and 12 assists in only 64 games, which is really good.

He hasn't had the best start to the season for Real Sociedad, no doubt about that. He has been a little bit off it, in that it took a while for him to find the back of the net for them, but his international record is outstanding.

Lamine Yamal has 25 goal contributions in 16 games for Barcelona this season, and 11 goals and 14 assists in 37 games for Spain. So we all know what to expect from Lamine Yamal in this game. Interestingly enough, will Nico Williams come back in?

He missed out the other night through illness, and it's still unclear whether he is going to be available or whether he's going to be on the bench. Laporte was also ill the other night.

That's my point, really: they can miss these players. They're one of those international teams where you can make four, five or six changes. The pattern is so embedded in what they play, the brand of football, through the youth team and through the training sessions.

The quality obviously drops when you haven't got those top players, but the patterns of play are still the same. The players still know what they're doing.

It's generally going to be good enough to beat most other teams. I don't think Spain with an under-strength team would fancy their chances against the best teams, but in 90% of the games they play, if they put their second string out, they're going to win. That's just how it is. It's an interesting game.

I did the England post-match piece for Sports Mole last night, and I said that was not a performance that would leave the likes of Spain quaking in their boots for this game.

I think Spain are the big favourites, especially considering the players that they'll welcome back in and their form. The manager's outstanding, and what an international manager he has turned out to be for Spain.

It's a tough game for England. Topping the group from an English point of view would be great, but it was always about getting through to the next round.

It would have been a disaster really if England didn't manage to make it through. Spain were always going to be the favourites to top the group.

They're the favourites for the Nations League, and they're probably going to be the favourites for the next Euros and the next World Cup. That's just the way it is. Zubimendi was an interesting one for me the other night.

He's going through a difficult spell club-wise at Arsenal at the moment, but he was one of Spain's best players last time out.

Pedro Porro has had his problems at Tottenham, but on the international stage he turns into Cafu when he's playing for Spain.

He was outstanding at the World Cup. Cucurella, and Cubarsi has gone to a new level with Spain and with Barcelona as well. They're good defensively.

Rodri is missing, but Fabian Ruiz has been excellent this season for PSG, and he's always excellent for Spain.

Someone else I did just want to mention, lastly, is Alex Baena, who had his chance at the World Cup with Nico Williams having his fitness problems.

He has five goals and four assists this season for Atletico Madrid, and he caused Man United all sorts of problems when they played against him in the Champions League.

He's an outstanding wide technical player, 25 years of age. If Nico Williams can't play, then he is some player off the left for them as well.

So there are worrying signs. If I'm honest, I do think Spain win this game, but I think it'll be relatively close, just like the last game was.

It was a really good spectacle last time out between these two sides. But Spain are the best team in the world at the moment. I expect them to win this, top the group and, to be honest, I expect them to win the Nations League as well this year.
