The second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Bellingham almost flicked in Rogers’s cross on 56 minutes and from the corner that came after, Kane nodded in a header at the back post from Lewis Hall’s cross. All said, the defending was woeful but there was nothing wrong with the finish.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and said he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

“It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel said: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

But on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

“We had these experiences together and we had a big tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

“We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”

We played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find new words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

[Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We had a strong qualification, strong World Cup and strong camp. All four matches were on a high level. The camp throughout from the first day was on the highest level. You learn every day together. We grew stronger.

I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Everyone showed he was willing to give everything for the team and for the shirt. The guys who were with us for the World Cup set the standards high, made everyone feel welcome and everyone had a good camp.

He’s the best England player evert to wear the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him. And he’s only getting better.

A perfect night for me personally and also for the team. It’s been a tough camp, a long camp with some difficult games so it’s nice to finish it off all together. An extremely proud evening for me.

You saw some fantastic football out there tonight. The way we’re moving, the one-touch stuff, a fantastic ball from Elliot to Morgan and then a first time cross which was as good as it gets. As a striker you’re just waiting for those opportunities.

It started in the first game [reaching a higher level] although the result didn’t go for us. First game after a tournament, obviously this was a four-game camp, we had to find it [a higher level] and find it quickly. That’s the most pleasing thing.

This is the England team. There’s always going to be competition for places. It’s about taking the opportunity whether it’s 90 minutes, five minutes, whatever it was, make the most of it. You’re seeing that, everyone wants to be part of this. That’s only going to make us better for sure.

[Now for cap 126 next month?] That would be nice for sure.

Because places between teams who finish on the same points in the first instance are decided on head-to-heads, Croatia will have to beat England 8-0 at Wembley next month to have any hope of stopping them from qualifying for the quarter-finals.

The Arsenal forward is poised to come in for Anthony Gordon, who has started in the three matches during the Nations League international break. Trent Alexander-Arnold is also due to play at right-back, with Jarell Quansah moving to centre-back to cover for Ezri Konsa.

Alex Scott has been ruled out through injury, which has upset Bournemouth after he played in the win over Croatia at the weekend. Myles Lewis-Skelly is expected to get a recall to the team after playing against Czech Republic in Prague last week when England won 2-0. Morgan Rogers, who scored against Croatia, is in line to start in place of Bukayo Saka.

Probable England team: Pickford; Trent, Quansah, Guehi, Hall; Lewis-Skelly, Anderson; Rogers, Bellingham, Eze; Kane

Advertisement | GambleAware | 18+ Betting on the football tonight? Take a look at these tips and offers chosen by Telegraph Media Group

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of England vs Czech Republic from Wembley in the fourth and mercifully final round of fixtures in this sprawling Nations League international break. Tonight Harry Kane will win his 125th cap and equal Peter Shilton for England appearances.

Shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

England played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

In the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Given the attacking fluency in Rijeka, Thomas Tuchel must be tempted not to to ring the changes and replace seven or eight players. He will have to find replacements for the injured Alex Scott and Ezri Konsa, however, and Calvert Lewin, who has had seven minutes of action, Rio Ngumoha 19, Morgan Gibbs-White 27 and Jarrad Branthwaite one, may feel they deserve a fairer opportunity to show what they can do in a match.

#1407. Mary Fowler was offered a record $1million to return home and reunite with Nathan Cleary - but she said no

Published: 21:52 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 21:57 EST, 11 November 2026

A reported record-breaking pay offer and the chance to live closer to Nathan Cleary were not enough to bring Mary Fowler back to Australia.

The Matildas star remains at Manchester City after a reported $1million offer emerged as part of an ambitious plan to recruit Australian sport’s glamour couple to two clubs under the same ownership umbrella.

The proposal could have offered a solution to the long-distance relationship that keeps their careers on opposite sides of the world.

For battling NRL franchise Wests Tigers, it was an extraordinary bid to prise one of rugby league’s biggest names away from Penrith.

According to News Corp, Tigers owner Holman Barnes Group proposed a combined package worth $9million, including a $1million marquee contract for Fowler to join the Central Coast Mariners women’s team.

The group had acquired the Mariners women’s side, opening the door to a recruitment pitch spanning two sports.

Mary Fowler remains at Manchester City despite a reported $1million offer to return to Australian football

A proposed recruitment package would have brought Fowler to the Central Coast Mariners and Cleary to Wests Tigers

Fowler returned to Australia in October to support Cleary following two operations

Under the reported proposal, Cleary would have joined the Tigers and Fowler would have returned to NSW on what would be the highest salary in A-League Women history.

But the blockbuster homecoming did not materialise.

Fowler, 23, is contracted to Manchester City until 2028, meaning any move would also require an agreement with the English club over her release.

She has built a formidable profile away from the pitch, with News Corp reporting that her multi-year Adidas deal is worth $10million.

Her other commercial work includes a L’Oréal Paris ambassadorship and Chobani’s national ‘Game Changer’ campaign.

The couple’s long-distance relationship attracted renewed attention in October when Fowler returned to Australia to support Cleary as he recovered from two operations.

She withdrew from Matildas friendlies against Germany and Haiti for personal reasons in October, prompting questions about her sudden absence.

Football Australia said the decision followed discussions between Fowler, Manchester City and Matildas staff.

Fowler’s commercial pulling power extends well beyond football, with  her multi-year Adidas deal worth $10million

Fowler became L’Oréal Paris’s first female athlete ambassador for Australia and New Zealand in 2024, adding a major beauty partnership to her growing profile

Fowler fronts Chobani’s national ‘Game Changer’ campaign, appearing across billboards, public transport and digital advertising as the brand launches its high-protein drinks

Should athletes choose love or loyalty to their teams when faced with life-changing offers?

Teammate Hayley Raso revealed the news had caught her by surprise.

‘I haven’t spoken to Mary. I only just found out the news myself,’ Raso said.

‘Obviously, Mary’s a really valuable player for our team, so it’s sad that she’s not here at this camp, but obviously, she has to take care of some personal circumstances.’

Cleary had fractured his fibula and dislocated his ankle during Penrith’s preliminary final loss to Newcastle, with a bone breaking through the skin.

He also had a fracture in his other foot.

Panthers chairman Greg Alexander later explained that the damage, while confronting, could have been worse.

‘The tibia didn’t break, no fracture in the tibia, which was fantastic news,’ Alexander told SEN.

‘In terms of the horrific injury that Nathan suffered, it was as good as could be expected without the double fracture.’

Cleary has since reportedly passed up another offer to remain with the club where he won four consecutive premierships.

The NRL expansion club the PNG Chiefs proposed a package worth up to $8.4million over three years, according to News Corp.

That reportedly included $6million in tax-free playing payments and a potential $2.4million in third-party endorsements.

Nine reported that Cleary told the Chiefs he intended to stay at Penrith, where he was expected to sign a two-year extension through to the end of 2029.

#1405. The 10 players Tottenham let go in the summer – & how they’re faring elsewhere

There was a lot of focus on the players coming through the door, but Tottenham Hotspur also let a lot of players go this past summer.

Ten players left in the summer permanently with another seven out on loan, as Roberto De Zerbi reshaped his squad following last year’s relegation scare.

And so we’re catching up on how those permanent exits have gone.

This is already looking like one that got away.

Following the Van Hecke/Vuskovic swap deal, it is the latter that has looked the better this season and has played a starring role in Fabian Hurzeler’s impressive Brighton team.

He has started all 10 games for the Seagulls, missing just two minutes of action so far this season, and has all the attributes that you would want from a modern centre-back.

Spurs reportedly inserted a clause into the contract but that was only to match any accepted bid rather than a pre-determined amount. If he continues like this, Brighton would not want to sell him for anything but a huge fee.

Another centre-back that left Spurs in the summer was Christian Romero, who took his sometimes maybe good, sometimes maybe red card attitude to Spain.

Moving to Atletico seems to have served him well as he is now under the rule of ‘takes no s**t’ Diego Simeone.

He’s played eight games for the Madrid side so far, who are third in La Liga and have the joint best defence.

Plenty of English players have enjoyed trips abroad but Djed Spence has yet to make a real mark at Inter.

He missed the first five games as he came back to fitness following the World Cup and was phased into the team, rather than given a starting spot from the off.

He did start the Milan derby, which Inter lost 3-1 to Ruben Amorim’s Milan, but was trusted to start again the following game, providing an assist in a 2-0 win over Como.

Even after the arrival of Omar Marmoush and Savinho, Spurs’ forward line looks the weakest area of the team. If only they had access to a striker scoring for fun.

Yes, it’s the Championship but Will Lankshear’s 13 goals in 13 games for Middlesbrough is hugely impressive and the 21-year-old already looks like an England star of the future. Keep scoring at that rate and he may well get a call-up sooner rather than later.

Spurs sold him for around £20m which looks on the low side already.

If Spurs fans were annoyed about the sale of Lankshear, they were probably less unhappy with the transfer of Alejo Veliz.

Spurs fans would do well to pick him out of a lineup for he only played eight games for Tottenham since joining in 2023, amounting to 45 minutes in total.

He’s been on loan to both Espanyol and Rosario Central but moved permanently to Esporte Clube Bahia in Brazil.

The 23-year-old has got four goals in his 15 games for the club so far.

It was not just Lankshear who left Spurs for Middlesbrough as defender Phillips also made the same journey in the summer.

He had plenty of Championship experience having spent the past two seasons in the division on loan at Stoke but Middlesbrough signed him in the summer for an initial fee of £7m.

He has since become a key member of Kim Hellberg’s side. He also scored a last-minute winner in a 4-3 thriller against Norwich, which is a great way to endear yourself to the fans.

Having been on loan spells to three different clubs, Manor Solomon left Spurs permanently in the summer to join West Ham.

Given the number 10 shirt for the Hammers’ first season back in the Championship, he started well with a goal on his debut but has faded in the last few weeks.

West Ham have been on a terrible run too with him in the side, having failed to win the last four games he was involved in.

Another academy product let go is midfielder Devine, who has joined Preston.

It’s fair to say, Preston are stinking the gaff out in the Championship and are bottom, having won two games all season.

Devine has played in all but one match so far, although it took 11 games to register his first goal involvement. Preston did, though, pull off an upset against promotion candidates Southampton in their most recent game, so maybe their fortunes are starting to change.

Long-time youth product Dane Scarlett left in the summer having never managed to properly break into the Spurs first team.

He played 27 games for Spurs, of which 11 were in the Premier League for a combined 61 minutes, and has been out on loan here, there and everywhere.

He was most recently at Hibernian but has now joined Leyton Orient permanently. Since making the short trip, he’s got one goal in eight League One games.

The player most likely to give successive managers a migraine left Tottenham this summer and headed for Ajax.

He was unable to play for the first seven games due to visa issues and even then was only gradually brought into the team, with his debut being just eight minutes long.

He finally started in Ajax’s final game before the international break but was hooked on the hour mark.

#1403. Ranking 12 of Zlatan Ibrahimovic’s best goals in order of ridiculousness

Zlatan Ibrahimovic scored over 500 goals during his career, but it’s not so much the number of goals he scored that made him special as the outrageous way in which he scored them.

After spells with Juventus, Barcelona and Manchester United, Ibrahimovic continued to prove that he can score in ways which appear physically impossible before finally hanging up his boots at the end of the 2022-23 campaign.

Over his illustrious career, he built quite a catalogue of absurd goals. And now we’ve ranked just some of his most outrageous ones in order of ridiculousness.

Because this is Zlatan, it looks like a standard goal. Straightforward. Run of the mill.

But wait for the replay and see how high the ball is when Zlatan strikes it; how he twists his body; how he uses the outside of his boot to get it through the crowd and inside the post.

It’s bottom of our list, but a fine example of Zlatan making the extraordinary look ordinary.

﻿

When coaches tell you to “put your foot through it”, they probably mean something like this.

For Inter Milan, Ibrahimovic shows us the devastating consequence of mixing power with accuracy.

﻿

Ibrahimovic gets across the defender man-marking him and bullets the ball into the roof of the net – with the side of his boot, no less.

GOAL OF THE DAY :23’ : Zlatan Ibrahimović vs Olympique de Marseille (2-2)Ligue 1 2013-2014 – 8ème journée pic.twitter.com/7gb6hQptRU

— Jeunesse PSG (@psgfans18) March 20, 2018

Ibrahimovic has more or less standardised this move to the point of us no longer being surprised when he pulls it off, but at the time, when he was playing for Jose Mourinho’s Inter, it was something never witnessed before.

Ibrahimovic stands tall and lets the ball drop into his midriff. In a move we have now seen several times, he somehow generates enough power to send the ball into the top corner despite facing away from the goal.

GOAL OF THE DAY⚽️:10’: Zlatan Ibrahimović vs SC Bastia (victoire 4-0)@Ligue1Conforama 2013/2014 – 10ème journée pic.twitter.com/qIkAhGeRoh

— Jeunesse PSG (@psgfans18) April 8, 2018

A disgustingly good strike from distance. We don’t know what’s more ridiculous: the fact Ibrahimovic decided to strike the ball first time or the fact he manages to put so much whip on the ball.

﻿

Against Ronald Koeman’s Benfica in a pre-season encounter, eyes turned away from Juventus’ gorgeous kit for a moment as Ibrahimovic scored this delightful goal.

The ball isn’t in an ideal place for a strike, but Ibrahimovic pulls the trigger regardless and catches the keeper off guard from distance.

Even Gianluigi Buffon didn’t know what to do when Zlatan pulled off a swinging backheel kick in the Euro 2004 group stage match.

Very few players would have the wherewithal to even think of doing this. Even fewer would be able to pull it off.

Ibrahimović is the only player to appear twice in this thread.pic.twitter.com/LTd83ImyQ5

— GoalScorer Challenge (@GoalscorerC) June 12, 2020

First, Ibrahimovic turns the defender on the halfway line with a flick. Then he chases down the ball and shoulder-barges the pursuing defender to the floor.

This is all before the big Swede brings the ball into his control and slams it high past the goalkeeper at his near post.

﻿

In a match billed as the ‘California Classico’, this wasn’t a bad way for Ibrahimovic to score his 500th career goal.

"I’m happy for Toronto as they’ll be remembered as my 500th victim."

Ibrahimovic's 500th career goal was typically ridiculous.pic.twitter.com/7fkpKPWqvk

— Planet Football (@planetfutebol) June 5, 2023

Ibrahimovic hit the world stage with this goal.

Its ridiculousness stems from him beating the entire backline – including the same player twice – in such a short space, before coolly slotting the ball into the net and wheeling away in celebration. It’s so good we wrote an entire article about it.

﻿

In a list full of outrageous goals, this must be the most ridiculous of all. It was an overhead kick from 30 yards, FFS.

#OnThisDay in 2012, Zlatan Ibrahimovic did something which, let's face it, only he can do. That thirty-odd yard overhead kick against England. Sizzled Joe Hart's brain in his head like it was a fried egg. Sensational. pic.twitter.com/Wj7vmmBB8n

— MUNDIAL (@MundialMag) November 14, 2020

#1402. Crystal Palace: Four signings that would be perfect for Thomas Frank in January

Thomas Frank is set to replace Pierre Sage as the manager of Crystal Palace and will be aiming to turn their fortunes around.

Palace are bottom of the table and have shown serious signs of decline this season after the loss of Oliver Glasner in the dugout. Sage just wasn’t able to get the same kind of results as his predecessor over his short reign and has paid the price early.

All Palace can hope now is that they’ve appointed Brentford Frank rather than Tottenham Frank. It could be an ideal opportunity for him to get back on track and redeem his reputation.

But he’ll need all the help he can get to turn this around.

Under Sage, Palace have had comfortably the worst defensive record in the Premier League, conceding 24 goals after 10 games.

Losing their two best centre-backs in successive transfer windows in 2026 hasn’t helped. Marc Guehi went to Manchester City in January before Maxence Lacroix joined Chelsea in the summer.

Palace have failed to replace them adequately. They’ve brought in a couple of temporary solutions on loan but need to think about the long term.

They might have to be savvy in January to find a good solution, looking beyond the usual places.

One player they’ve been linked with recently is Lecce defender Gabriel, who would be a good fit for Frank’s tactics if they can win the race.

Good in the air and alert when the ball’s on the ground, the 21-year-old is ready for his next step and a Premier League move could suit.

During his time at Brentford, Frank was able to help plenty of players improve and Gabriel could be the right kind of defender to work with in the short and long term.

Frank was delighted to sign Gallagher for Spurs last January. He won’t have been so delighted to be sacked four weeks later.

But with Gallagher falling behind in importance for Spurs this season, could he become available again?

If so, he could bring fresh energy into the Palace midfield. Adam Wharton hasn’t quite looked the same player there this season and could probably use some help to get back to his usual standards.

Gallagher could easily do the legwork. He also knows what it takes to play for Palace after impressing there on loan from Chelsea during the 2021-22 season, a spell that included eight goals from 39 games.

Palace could also do with improving their attack. Jean-Philippe Mateta is clearly unsettled, Jorgen Strand Larsen hasn’t got going and Eddie Nketiah isn’t up to scratch either.

Could Richarlison be worth a call? He’s been completely frozen out by Spurs, where Frank had a better opinion of him than Roberto De Zerbi does.

It’s anyone’s guess what Richarlison wants as his next step. But going to Palace would allow him to link back up with a familiar manager and stay in London, too.

The Brazilian is versatile enough to play as a lone striker or in support of another if Palace want to persist with Strand Larsen, Mateta or Nketiah as well.

If Frank wants to look further back, to happier times with Brentford, he might have a hard time convincing anyone to reunite with him given the current positions of both clubs.

But considering Hickey isn’t starting regularly for Brentford, with Michael Kayode ahead of him in the hierarchy at right-back, we wonder if he might be tempted.

Frank rated Hickey highly during their time together. It’s easy to forget the versatile full-back is still only 24.

Palace had to replace Daniel Munoz this summer and his successor Anan Khalaili has been hit and miss so far. Hickey would be someone Frank could trust to offer more security at wing-back.

Frank shut the door on a Brentford exit for Hickey before but what if he turned out to be the man to get him out of the Gtech Community Stadium after all?

#1399. 18 more England records Harry Kane could break after becoming all-time caps leader

Harry Kane. The most-capped England player of all time and the top scorer for his country too. He might just be his nation’s best ever representative, you know.

Sure, he wasn’t around for the World Cup win in 1966. But when that’s the only major honour England have ever won, you can’t exactly knock players down for not replicating it.

With someone like Kane, you just have to look at the numbers to realise what he’s achieved. More often than not, he passes the eye test as well. He’s been a huge influence for England at some tournaments over the years.

And now, after his cap against Croatia on Thursday, he’s played in more England internationals than anyone else. A whole 126 of them.

Kane can proudly boast the all-time appearance and goal records for England, which are the big two. He also holds the records for most appearances as captain, most appearances at the Euros, most caps and goals while playing for a foreign club, most goals in a calendar year and so on.

But there are still more he could break. He’s 33 now, but still in good shape. Come on, this is the reigning Ballon d’Or winner we’re talking about.

So here are some records that could be in his sights over the rest of his international career.

Kane’s already a joint-record holder for this one and, unlike the three old-timers he shares the record with, he’s done it twice.

The record is six, first set by Tinsley Lindley in the 1880s and since matched by Jimmy Windridge in the 1900s, Tommy Lawton in the 1930s and Kane in both 2019 and between December 2022 and June 2023.

Steve Bloomer, from the 1890s, has the record of scoring in 10 consecutive appearances, but there were fixtures he didn’t play in in between.

So Kane is one of the four record holders for most consecutive England games scored in – and he’s not far off doing it for a third time.

He’s scored in every England game since the World Cup and so is currently on a run of five. All he needs to do is score against Spain on Sunday and then in England’s first game of the March international break to become the first man to score in seven consecutive England fixtures.

The next tournament England will be turning their attention to qualifying for is Euro 2028. And yes, they have to qualify, despite being co-hosts.

Kane is already a few days older than the current record holder for the oldest England scorer in a Euros qualifying match – Kyle Walker at 33 years and 104 days – and he’s going to score at least once in qualifying, right?

Should England make it to Euro 2028, you’d imagine Kane would still be an important player by then.

It’d be his fourth Euros with England, enough for him to overtake the eight players he’s currently level with. The only other among them still active in international football is Jordan Henderson, but we see Kane as a safer bet to be in the squad by then.

The next Euros would also be the seventh consecutive tournament Kane had represented England at. He’s currently tied with Henderson, Sol Campbell and Wayne Rooney on six in a row.

Kane will be 34 years and 317 days old when Euro 2028 kicks off. It won’t make him the oldest player to represent England at the tournament – that’s goalkeeper Peter Shilton at 38 – but he would be the oldest outfield player, presuming no one older than him would be in the squad.

Only Henderson and Dan Burn were older than him in the World Cup squad and we’d be a bit surprised if they were still sticking around for the next tournament.

The current record is held by Stuart Pearce at 34 years and 63 days old.

Surely Kane has at least one more goal in him at the Euros, even if we are looking 18 months into the future here.

If he does, he’d overtake Alan Shearer, who he’s currently tied with on seven, as England’s top scorer at the Euros. In fact, unless anyone was to get there before him, only Cristiano Ronaldo and Michel Platini would still be above him for the competition as a whole.

In the event of him scoring at Euro 2028, Kane would have a goal to his name from five consecutive international tournaments.

His only equivalent on four is Michael Owen.

And whenever that hypothetical Euros goal would come, Kane would be guaranteed to beat Trevor Brooking’s record as England’s oldest scorer at the competition.

Sir Trevor was 31 years old when he set the record, an age Kane is already past.

A bit more ambitious here, but the current record for most goals at a single Euros tournament by an Englishman is five, set by Alan Shearer in 1996.

It’s not that far out of reach, is it? Sure, only nine players have done it for any country before, but if England were to go far, there’d be enough games for Kane to have a crack at it.

He consistently steps up at the World Cup for his country and there’s no reason why he couldn’t at the Euros too. His personal best at the tournament is four in 2021, for the delayed 2020 edition.

And like Shearer in ’96, he’d have home advantage to carry him through as well.

File this one under unlikely, but maybe not as much as it sounds.

Onto the next tournament cycle and we could imagine a future in which Kane is still involved for the build-up to the 2030 World Cup.

He recently said it was “fairly realistic” that he’d still be an England player by the time of the next World Cup, but of course, England would have to get there first.

The current oldest scorer for England in a World Cup qualifying match is Teddy Sheringham, who was 35 years and 187 days old.

Details of the qualification process for the 2030 World Cup aren’t out yet, but Kane will turn 35 in the summer of 2028 and if he scores towards the end of a qualification campaign, he’d be able to surpass Sheringham.

If Kane does make it to the next World Cup, and plays for England at least once in every year in between, he’ll set a new record for the most consecutive years of appearances for the Three Lions.

2026 is the 12th consecutive year in which he’s appeared for his country. The record of 15 is currently shared by David Seaman and Rio Ferdinand.

As long as his England career continues uninterrupted, Kane will join them in 2029 and beat them in 2030.

Kane is already England’s top scorer at the World Cup, but he hasn’t played the most games at it for his country.

The record is Jordan Pickford’s with 19. Kane is one behind on 18.

There’s every chance both of them will be at the World Cup next time, but there’s half a suspicion Pickford could be phased out by then – especially if someone like James Trafford develops over the next few years.

A successor to Kane up front isn’t quite as obvious just yet and so he might be relied upon for longer, giving him a chance to overtake his long-time teammate.

The oldest scorer for England at a World Cup finals game was Tom Finney. He was 36 years and 64 days old when he scored against the Soviet Union in 1958.

Kane will be more than 250 days older than that by the time the next World Cup commences, so he’d just need a goal at any time to beat it.

Kane’s recent contract renewal with Bayern Munich means he’ll be playing in Germany until 2029.

He’s played for England 41 times since he left Tottenham Hotspur and the Premier League behind in 2023.

That means he only needs to play 14 more times to equal, or 15 times to beat, David Beckham’s record for the most caps earned while not playing club football in England.

55 of Beckham’s caps came after he left Manchester United to embark on a career with Real Madrid, LA Galaxy and AC Milan (he had retired from international football by the time he joined his last club, PSG).

You’d imagine Kane will play way more than 15 times for England between now and 2029.

Believe it or not, Kane hasn’t scored a hat-trick for England for five years now, last doing so in November 2021 against San Marino.

But it was his fifth international hat-trick and only Jimmy Greaves has more for England with six.

Could Kane get two more to overtake him? That might require some luck of the draw with qualifying for tournaments, pitting England against weaker teams, but he’s got enough time to try.

He does it often enough at club level, after all.

Even if he just gets one more hat-trick to match Greaves, he’d stand alone as the oldest hat-trick scorer for England.

That’s currently Jack Rowley at 31 years and 40 days old in 1949. It’s been a long-standing record, but Kane would instantly set a new one if he was to score an international hat-trick at any point from now.

Another one that might need some luck of the draw, but Kane has played seven times against Croatia in his England career, including on his record-breaking cap.

The only man to have played against a single, non-British opponent more is Alan Ball, who played eight times against West Germany between 1965 and 1975.

England and Croatia seem to meet every other week, so although the international schedule beyond this break remains unclear, there’s every chance Kane will cross paths with them again.

On a similar note, the most anyone has scored against a single non-British opponent for England is eight, by Vivian Woodward against Austria between 1908 and 1909.

Kane’s most common victims have been Albania (seven goals) and Croatia (six goals). If he plays against either of them again once or twice, he might fancy his chances.
